body: ## Third-highest pre-1980 share on our list

In the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), 4,133 of Holliston's 5,697 housing units, 72.5%, were built before 1980. Only two of the 50 towns we serve have a higher share, and the middle town sits at 57.2%. The median Holliston home was built in 1966, the 10th-oldest median on our list, compared with 1975 for the middle town. Only 417 units, 7.3%, have gone up since 2010. The ACS puts the population at 14,902, the 21st-largest of the 50 towns.
## The 1960 to 1979 block

The largest age band in town is 1960 to 1979, with 2,147 units (37.7%). Another 933 (16.4%) were built from 1940 to 1959, and 1,053 (18.5%) date from 1939 or earlier. In general, a house built before modern insulation and air-sealing practices became common can have a different heating load from a new house of the same size. The only reliable way to size a replacement is to measure the actual house.
## Gas on top, oil in the middle

Utility gas heats 3,257 occupied homes (58.6%), the 11th-highest gas share of the 50 towns and well above the 41.9% of the middle town. Fuel oil heats 1,546 (27.8%), against 36.5% for the middle town. A gas household's replacement choice is usually between the same fuel again and a heat pump added alongside. An oil household has more to weigh: another oil system, gas if a main reaches the property, or a heat pump.
## Owners, mostly

Owners occupy 4,889 of Holliston's 5,562 occupied homes (87.9%), and 673 households (12.1%) rent. So most decisions about repair and replacement sit with the people living in the house. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $588,000, close to the $579,150 of the middle town. Electricity heats 562 homes (10.1%) and bottled gas 174 (3.1%).
## Shoe factories and a map location

Holliston was first settled by Europeans in 1659 and was incorporated on December 3, 1724, when the western part of Sherborn became a town. The name honors Thomas Hollis of London, a benefactor of Harvard College, and the first town meeting was held at the house of Timothy Leland on December 23, 1724. The town's Mudville neighborhood claims to be the setting of the 1888 poem "Casey at the Bat." The town was once the largest producer of shoes in the United States, and empty factories of the Goodwill Shoe Company remain on Water Street, many now used as artists' studios.

The town covers 19.0 square miles, of which 1.73% is water, and the Charles River passes near the southern part of town. It lies 21.6 miles west of Boston, within short driving distance of Interstate 495 and the Massachusetts Turnpike, with Routes 16 and 126 passing through it. Holliston is the only Middlesex County town that borders both Norfolk and Worcester counties. Before European settlement the area belonged to the Nipmuc, and a village called Mucksquit stood near the site of the Morse family farm, today known as Lake Winthrop. The town retains two official historic districts.
## Which utility serves your address

We have not confirmed the town's electric utility, so we do not name one here. Your electric bill shows which utility serves your address, and that utility is the one that runs any heat pump rebate. Our [heat pump page](/cities/holliston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the 2026 Mass Save terms and what to confirm.

faq.q: Does the age of Holliston housing change which heating system I need?
faq.a: It can. The ACS shows 72.5% of units were built before 1980, with the largest group from 1960 to 1979. It does not say how those houses were built or altered, and insulation, air leakage and distribution differ from house to house. A measured heat loss settles the size.

faq.q: Is gas available on my Holliston street?
faq.a: Gas heats 58.6% of occupied homes in town, but whether a main runs past your house depends on the street. The gas company can tell you, and so can we at the estimate. The answer decides whether a like-for-like replacement, a conversion or a heat pump makes the most sense.

faq.q: Which electric utility serves Holliston, and does it matter for rebates?
faq.a: We have not confirmed it, so check your electric bill. The bill names the utility, and the heat pump program you can use follows from that name. Confirm the terms with the utility before you commit to equipment.

faq.q: Are most Holliston homes owned or rented?
faq.a: Owned. The ACS 2022 counts 4,889 owner-occupied households (87.9%) and 673 renter households (12.1%), and Holliston ranks 37th of 50 towns for renter share. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $588,000.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Gas heats 3,257 occupied Holliston homes (58.6%) and oil 1,546 (27.8%). With 72.5% of units built before 1980, the pipes, radiators and chimney get a look before a new boiler or furnace is sized.
body: ## Gas first, oil second

Holliston ranks 11th of 50 towns for gas and 33rd for oil, so gas is the usual starting point. Whether it is available at a given house depends on the street. Electricity heats 562 homes (10.1%, level with the middle town), bottled or tank gas heats 174 (3.1%), and wood heats 23.
## The older end of the stock

The ACS 2022 counts 1,053 units built in 1939 or earlier, and 933 more from 1940 to 1959. A boiler or furnace swap in a house that old often means checking whether the pipes, radiators, ducts and chimney suit the new unit. The 1960 to 1979 block is the largest at 2,147 units, and it brings a different question: how much heat the house loses, which a heat-loss calculation answers before sizing.
## Why the pre-1980 share matters

Holliston ranks 3rd of 50 towns for homes built before 1980: 4,133 of 5,697 units, against 57.2% for the middle town. That puts a large number of boilers and furnaces in houses that were planned before modern air-sealing became common. The practical effect is that an old nameplate is a poor guide to what the house needs now, and the load calculation does the work instead.
## Smaller fuel groups

A homeowner with an electric-resistance house can look at the [heat pump option](/cities/holliston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits). A propane household can price its tank fuel against the alternatives. Neither group is large here, but each may find more value in a change than a gas household would.
## Gas work and paperwork

Putting in a new gas boiler or furnace is a permitted job. The permit comes from a licensed plumber or gas fitter, and the installation is inspected afterward. Ask the building department if your job is unusual.
## Renters

Holliston's 673 renter households fall under the State Sanitary Code: in the heating season, 68 F is the minimum during the day and 64 F the minimum overnight (105 CMR 410.201). Who pays for heat follows the lease, and the landlord pays if the lease is silent. This is general information, not legal advice.
## When the heat fails
Call (508) 786-8755 at any hour. A breakdown is treated as an emergency whatever the time, and a free written estimate comes before the work.

faq.q: Should I repair or replace my Holliston boiler?
faq.a: A single failed part on a fairly young boiler is usually worth repairing. An old boiler with repeated faults, or a safety defect found on inspection, usually calls for replacement. We examine the unit and the house and put the options in writing.

faq.q: Can I replace oil with gas in Holliston?
faq.a: Only where gas is available at your address. Oil heats 1,546 homes in town, and for those owners a conversion may be worth pricing alongside a new oil unit and a heat pump. The estimate can compare all three.

faq.q: Who pulls the permit for a new boiler?
faq.a: Your contractor normally does. The work has to be done by a licensed plumber or gas fitter, and it is inspected when finished. Ask before you sign.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Holliston is mostly detached houses (4,468 units, 78.4%), with 507 homes in buildings of five or more units. Detached houses can take central air or ductless systems, and many older homes were built without central air.
body: ## Cooling mostly single-family houses

The ACS 2022 counts 4,468 detached houses in Holliston, 78.4% of units, plus 340 attached townhouses (6.0%). Buildings of five or more units hold 507 units (8.9%), and 30 are mobile homes. A detached house gives the most options: an outdoor condenser fits more easily, and ducts or a ductless system can reach most rooms. Townhouses and apartments can be more limited.
## Homes from 2000 on

The ACS counts 649 units built in 2000 or later (11.4%), including 417 from 2010. Newer houses are more likely to have ducts designed with cooling in mind, which can make a condenser replacement straightforward. Many older homes were built without central air, and a ducted retrofit can be hard to fit, which is when ductless becomes attractive.
- **Ducted central air:** best with sound, adequately sized ducts.
- **Ductless mini-split:** for additions, upper floors and houses without ducts.
- **Heat pump:** heats and cools from one system, as covered on the [heat pump page](/cities/holliston/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## The 1960 to 1979 houses

Holliston's largest age band is 1960 to 1979, at 2,147 units (37.7%). For houses from those decades, the question is whether the attic, windows and any existing ducts help or hinder a cooling system, and a visit settles it. The median home dates to 1966.
## Small buildings
Two-unit buildings hold 81 Holliston units and buildings of three or four hold 271. Whoever owns the yard and the electrical panel decides where an outdoor unit can go.
## Sizing

Too big a unit cycles on and off and removes humidity poorly. Cooling a house in July also depends on the attic, the windows and the shade, which is why two neighboring houses of the same size can need different equipment. Too small a unit runs flat out and still falls behind in a heat wave.
## Before you call

If cooling stops, check the thermostat, the breaker and the filter, then call (508) 786-8755. A technician can usually tell by inspection whether the fault is a frozen coil, a clogged drain or an electrical part.

faq.q: Can I add air conditioning without ductwork?
faq.a: Often yes. A ductless mini-split uses a small indoor unit connected to an outdoor unit by a thin line, so no ducts are needed. One head cools one room, and multi-head systems can serve more space.

faq.q: When should I replace instead of repair my air conditioner?
faq.a: When the unit is old, the repair cost is high or the fault is in the compressor or coil. A technician can tell you which case you are in. We give a written estimate before any work starts.

faq.q: Is a Holliston house from the 1960s hard to cool?
faq.a: Not by age alone. The town has 2,147 units from 1960 to 1979, and ducts, insulation and sun exposure vary within the group. A load check of your own house gives the real answer.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Holliston's electric utility is not confirmed in our records, so the rebate path depends on the utility serving your address. Oil heats 1,546 homes here and 4,133 units predate 1980, so weatherization status matters for most projects.
body: ## Start with your electric bill

Which utility serves Holliston is something we have not confirmed, so we do not say whether Mass Save applies. If your utility is municipal, Mass Save generally reaches only gas-heated homes and the utility has its own program. Check the bill, then confirm with the utility.
## The Mass Save headline

For homes that qualify, Mass Save's 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500, with weatherization required first. Details sit on the [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Which Holliston houses change the most

The ACS 2022 counts 1,546 oil-heated homes (27.8%), 562 on electricity (10.1%) and 174 on bottled gas (3.1%). Those are the cases where a heat pump replaces something burned or a resistance system. Gas, at 3,257 homes (58.6%), is by far the largest group, and for these homes the usual idea is a heat pump added beside the furnace or boiler, with the old system doing the coldest days.
## Age against the weatherization test

Holliston has 649 units from 2000 or later (11.4%), including 417 from 2010, and those meet the age route. The 4,133 units built before 1980 (72.5%) are where a Home Energy Assessment is likelier to decide matters, and 915 units from 1980 to 1999 fall in between. Holliston ranks 3rd of 50 for the pre-1980 share, so this question comes up here more than in most towns.
## House types

Most Holliston heat pumps would be outdoor units beside a detached house, since there are 4,468 of them (78.4%). The 340 townhouses and 507 units in buildings of five or more are likelier to need permission for outdoor equipment. The ACS also counts 30 mobile homes sit in the mix as well.
## Before you plan around a rebate

Because we have not confirmed the utility, the electric bill, not the town name, is the document to check before you plan a purchase around any rebate. Once you know the utility, ask it which program covers your fuel and what its terms are for the current year.
## Sizing

A heat pump sized too small leaves rooms cold in January, and one sized too large cycles more than it should. We measure the heating load before quoting. The [air conditioning page](/cities/holliston/air-conditioning-installation-repair) covers the cooling side.

faq.q: Does Mass Save apply to my Holliston house?
faq.a: It depends on the utility that serves your address, which we have not confirmed for Holliston. Check your electric bill and ask that utility which heat pump program applies to your home.

faq.q: Will a heat pump replace my oil boiler?
faq.a: Sometimes completely, sometimes partly. It depends on insulation, air leakage and sizing, which we assess first. Some houses keep the old system as a backup for the coldest days.

faq.q: My Holliston house dates from 1960 to 1979. Will it pass the weatherization test?
faq.a: Possibly, if a Home Energy Assessment recommends under $1,000 of work or earlier recommendations were completed. Holliston has 2,147 units from 1960 to 1979, so many owners will start with an assessment.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Holliston has 4,889 owner-occupied households and 16.4% of units from 1940 to 1959. Oil systems need an annual cleaning, gas equipment a yearly check, and heat pumps clean filters, ideally before the heating season.
body: ## An owner's calendar

With owners occupying 4,889 households, most maintenance decisions in Holliston belong to the people living in the house. Late summer suits heating service and spring suits cooling service. Any home with a fuel-burning appliance needs its vent checked, whether it is a detached house or one of the 30 mobile homes the ACS counts.
## By fuel
- **Oil:** heats 1,546 homes and needs cleaning every year.
- **Gas:** heats 3,257 homes and benefits from a yearly look at the burner and safety controls.
- **Heat pumps:** need clean filters and clear space around the outdoor unit.
- **Electric:** 562 homes, where wiring and controls still deserve a look.
- **Wood:** 23 homes, where the chimney is the item to inspect.
## Equipment age
The median Holliston home was built in 1966, and 933 units date from 1940 to 1959. Any equipment can wear out in time, and a service visit shows how much life is left in it.
## Small multi-unit buildings

The ACS puts 81 Holliston units in two-unit buildings and 271 in buildings of three or four. A boiler that serves several households can leave all of them cold when it fails, so a pre-season visit is cheap insurance.
## Landlords

Holliston has 673 renter households. A landlord's record of annual service shows the equipment was checked before the season began. That record is cheap to keep: a date, the work done and any parts flagged as worn.
## Why the schedule matters here

Holliston has 4,133 units built before 1980 (72.5%), the 3rd-highest share on our list. Equipment installed in houses of that age has often been running for decades, and each year the odds of a worn burner, a corroded flue or a failing circulator rise. A yearly visit is how those items get noticed before the first cold week, and the technician's notes help you decide when to replace rather than wait for a failure.
## Book a visit

Call (508) 786-8755. If the visit shows a cracked heat exchanger or a leaking boiler, a replacement may be needed, and the estimate is written and free. The [Holliston page](/cities/holliston) has the housing numbers.

faq.q: When should I schedule my boiler tune-up?
faq.a: Before the heating season, which starts around mid-September, so late summer is a good time. Oil systems get a yearly cleaning, and gas systems get a yearly inspection.

faq.q: Is service worthwhile on a heat pump?
faq.a: Yes. Filters need regular cleaning, outdoor units need clear space, and a technician should check the system periodically. Neglect can reduce comfort and shorten equipment life. Spring, before the first hot spell, is a good time for a heat pump that also cools.

faq.q: Does a 1960s Holliston boiler need more frequent service?
faq.a: Not on a fixed schedule, but it deserves a careful look each year. The town has 2,147 units from 1960 to 1979, and the technician's notes on worn parts help you plan a replacement before a failure forces one. Ask the technician to flag anything near the end of its life.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: In Holliston, 16.1% of units were built from 1980 to 1999 and 18.5% in 1939 or earlier. Older houses and tighter newer ones raise different indoor air questions.
body: ## Two kinds of house, two kinds of air

The ACS 2022 counts 915 Holliston units from 1980 to 1999 (16.1%), and 1,053 from 1939 or earlier. The largest band, 1960 to 1979, holds 2,147 units (37.7%), and 649 units date from 2000 or later. Older houses tend to leak air, which thins out some pollutants but also admits dust, pollen and damp basement air. Tighter, newer houses keep their moisture, cooking fumes and furnishing chemicals indoors when ventilation falls short.
## Water and humidity

Range hoods, bathroom fans and dryer vents are how moisture and fumes leave a house when they work properly. The ACS counts 135 vacant units in Holliston, a 2.4% vacancy rate, and a closed-up house can hold stale, humid air. Winter heating dries the air and summer brings humidity back, so a basement or a bedroom can call for a humidifier at one time of year and a dehumidifier at another. Finding the source of a damp spot matters more than treating the air around it. A musty smell near the cellar door is a reason to look for the moisture source before buying any equipment.
## Old wood and plaster

Wood floors, plaster and framing can respond to humidity swings, especially in older houses. Holliston has 933 units from 1940 to 1959 on top of the pre-1940 group, so protecting the building belongs on the list alongside protecting the people.
## The practical list
- **Filters:** a clean filter of a suitable grade can reduce dust moving through a ducted system.
- **Ventilation:** kitchen and bathroom fans should vent outdoors.
- **Ductwork:** leaky or dusty ducts matter, but cleaning helps only in some houses.
- **Fresh air:** a very tight house may need a ventilator rather than relying on leaks.
## The newest houses

Only 417 Holliston units (7.3%) have gone up since 2010, and 649 date from 2000 or later. Houses built in those years are often the tightest in town, so if you notice condensation on windows, lingering cooking smells or a stuffy bedroom, ventilation is the first thing to look at.
## Next steps
Call (508) 786-8755 to book an assessment. The [Holliston page](/cities/holliston) has the local numbers.

faq.q: Do older houses have worse air quality?
faq.a: Not necessarily. They tend to leak more, which dilutes some pollutants but admits dust and damp air. Tighter houses face other issues. With 4,133 pre-1980 units in town, an inspection of ducts, fans and moisture sources shows which applies to yours.

Sometimes, such as after renovation or visible contamination, and often not. Filter changes and an inspection usually come first. A carbon monoxide alarm and a flue check matter more for gas and oil equipment than a duct cleaning does.

faq.q: Can a vacant Holliston house develop air problems?
faq.a: It can, since a closed-up house may hold humid or stale air. With 135 vacant units in the ACS count, opening the house and checking for damp before anyone moves in is a sensible first step. A musty smell is a sign to look for moisture first.
